youtube.title: She bugged 5 presidents for 17 years. Lincoln caved 🦃 #shorts
youtube.caption:
The history of Thanksgiving starts with one woman who would NOT stop writing letters 🦃

Who's the person at YOUR Thanksgiving table who starts the politics talk? 👇

Parody · fictional chat. Based on history: Sarah Josepha Hale, editor of Godey's Lady's Book (and author of "Mary Had a Little Lamb"), campaigned for about 17 years for a national Thanksgiving, writing to Presidents Taylor, Fillmore, Pierce and Buchanan. In September 1863 she wrote to Abraham Lincoln; on 3 October 1863 he proclaimed a national day of Thanksgiving on the last Thursday of November.
